title: Nobody in the front seat, yet the Tesla keeps moving through Austin traffic
title_candidates: What it looks like to sit in the back of a Tesla as it drives itself
A Tesla owner rode in the back seat of his own car with no one in front
Nobody in the front seat, yet the Tesla keeps moving through Austin traffic
Tesla Model Y owners can now be passengers in their own car
The first feeling of sitting in a car you own as it drives you around
caption:
The person riding in the back seat of this Tesla owns the car. Nobody's in the front. It's driving itself through Austin, Texas, with no one touching the controls.

Tesla's robotaxi program now runs on the Model Y, meaning owners can sit in the back of a car they paid for and let it handle every turn and stop on its own. No steering, no pedals, no input. Just city traffic and an empty seat in front of you.

The Cybercab launched the following day. But the Model Y was already doing this first.
